summary: Describes a set of assembly-language subprograms at the University of California, Santa Barbara that let Fortran programs on its IBM 360/75 use the network. The routines sit between the programmer and the local Network Control Program. Each open socket has a completion code variable that tracks its status.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC describes helper routines that let UCSB Fortran programs use the network. Each open socket has a variable that identifies it and records how an operation ended.

subtitle: Assembly-language routines that let UCSB Fortran programs use the Network Control Program.

tldr.problem: Fortran programs at UCSB needed a callable way to use the local Network Control Program and operate on network sockets.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC documents subprograms for opening and closing sockets, sending and receiving data, checking status, identifying sockets, and sending signals.
tldr.outcome: The routines had been implemented at UCSB for Fortran programs compiled there. The document also describes message conventions for its Online System operators.

sections.title: An Interface for Fortran
sections.content: The subroutines described in RFC 119 were implemented at UCSB and make the Network accessible to Fortran programs running on its 360/75 through the Network Control Program (NCP). The routines are written in assembly language and can be called from a Fortran main program or subroutine compiled at UCSB.
sections.plainLanguage: Fortran programs use these helper routines to request network work from the local NCP. The routines were built for the UCSB computing environment.

sections.title: Sockets and Completion Codes
sections.content:
Each socket that is not closed has a unique completion-code variable. The variable identifies the local socket and holds the result code when an operation finishes; the RFC requires an INTEGER*4 variable.

Most routines wait without using CPU time until the NCP reports completion. The caller supplies a time limit in tenths of a second; if it expires, the operation remains pending and code 252 is returned.
sections.plainLanguage: A program keeps one result variable for each open socket. The variable tells the program whether the request worked or timed out while still pending.

sections.title: Network and Online-System Routines
sections.content:
OPEN can connect to a foreign socket, listen for a call, or accept a call after listening; CLOSE returns the local socket to the closed state. The WRITE and READ routines send and receive a chosen number of bits, while CHECK reports socket status immediately.

The RFC also describes ID and SIGNAL, plus routines for the Online System. Its operator messages use a one-byte operation code, a two-byte length, and text.
sections.plainLanguage: The routines cover connecting, listening, accepting, closing, sending, receiving, and checking a socket. Separate conventions describe messages for the Online System operators.
